editorial:
Imagine stepping into a strange, hand-drawn world where things aren't quite what they seem. You get thrown into a weird mix of fantasy and horror that feels like a fever dream. The story focuses on relationships that have completely fallen apart, using birds and strange figures to show how messy love and hate can be. The vibe is quirky and a bit unsettling, making you feel like you are watching a secret piece of art from another era. Since it is a short film, it doesn't waste any time getting you into its odd headspace.

What really grabs you is how the art looks. Even though not many things are moving on screen, the drawings are so detailed that they tell the story on their own. It is a bit slow in parts, but the weirdness makes up for it. You should check this out if you love indie animation that takes risks. Since it is an older gem, your best bet is to find a high-quality digital remaster.
endingExplained: The story wraps up by showing the total collapse of the characters' bonds. As the tension peaks, the figures shift into bird-like forms, proving that their relationships have truly gone to the birds. The final scenes show a cycle of conflict that cannot be fixed, leaving you with a feeling of irony. It ends with a sharp, sudden realization that the characters are trapped in their own bad habits, closing the loop on their strange journey.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves experimental shorts and unique art styles.
